description: Which charts suit this data? Answers 'what are good chart types for this dataset / model', 'what can I chart here', 'recommend some charts' for a semantic model in a Microsoft Fabric App built on Rayfin's data app template, in ONE call, from the model's real rows: reads its tables, columns, measures and relationships through the project's own `fabric-app-data` CLI, finds its natural views (measures by place, flows between places, measures over time, measures by category), queries each at its grain, keeps the measures that vary there, and asks the server's eligibility engine what fits each view. Replies view by view with the real counts (rows, places, periods, categories) and the chart types that fit, and saves each view's rows and DAX under .bic/data so generate_chart can build any of them next. Pass `views` to ask about your own groupings. Answer the person from this reply rather than from general knowledge. One eligibility call per view: metered like list_eligible_charts (free within an hourly allowance, usage credits beyond it) and needs the same licence. For one table you already hold, use list_eligible_charts.

alias.description: The semantic model's alias in fabric.yaml. Needed only when the active profile has more than one.

project_dir.description: The Fabric App project folder (holds fabric.yaml and node_modules). Defaults to the folder setup_fabric_app used, else the working directory or the one Fabric App folder directly inside it.

top.description: How many fitting chart types to name per view (default 6).

views.description: Groupings to ask about instead of the model's own. Omit to let the model's structure decide.

columns.description: The columns to group by, as Table[Column], e.g. ["Geography[Region]"].

dax.description: Or the view's own DAX query (EVALUATE ...), run as given.

measures.description: Measure names, e.g. ["Revenue"]. Omit to use the ones that vary most usefully at this grain.

name.description: A short name; the rows are saved as .bic/data/<name>.csv.

name: suggest_charts
title: Suggest charts for a semantic model
